image_description: A black and white close-up photograph of a cluster of whole figs resting on a wooden surface. The figs exhibit the characteristic pear-like or teardrop shape, with smooth skin showing subtle tonal variations and highlights indicating a matte texture. One fig in the foreground clearly displays the small ostiole (eye) at its base. No cut figs are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fruits clearly display the iconic pear/teardrop shape associated with figs. While color is absent due to the monochrome filter, the tonal values are consistent with the described skin types.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Smooth to slightly wrinkled texture with matte finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface reflection is diffuse rather than specular, indicating a matte finish. The skin appears smooth with very subtle undulations, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple figs in the cluster clearly show the tapering geometry from the wide body to the narrower neck/stem area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small ostiole (eye) at bottom of fruit.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fig in the lower-right center prominently features the small, distinct circular ostiole at its base.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Narrow stem end contrasting with broad rounded base.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The geometric contrast between the bulbous body and the tapered stem end is visually evident on several subjects.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cut cross-section reveals hollow interior filled with numerous tiny seeds.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All figs in the image are whole; there are no cut cross-sections visible to verify internal structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Sweet, pink to amber-colored fleshy pulp surrounding seeds.

Texture consistency (jam-like) is an internal property that cannot be visually confirmed without cutting the fruit.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific botanical classification of the fruit as 'fig' and rule out look-alikes like certain plums or dates.
To ensure individual fruits are topologically distinct and not merging/fusing into each other, a common AI artifact in clustered objects.
To assess the naturalness of the black and white conversion, grain structure, and lighting consistency.

focus_areas: Consistency of the ostiole feature across different angles
Naturalness of skin texture and highlights
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the boundaries where the figs touch each other and the wooden surface. AI generators often struggle with contact shadows and edge definition in clusters. Verify if the ostiole details are structurally consistent or if they appear painted on.
